source_text: Exemplum ac documentum nostri timoris et fidei ex ipsius Abrahae patriarchae fideli credulitate monstratur, qui repromissioni Dei mente simplici statim credidit et ideo ad iustitiam deputari ei condigna remuneratione commeruit. hoc Deus diligit, hoc adpetit, hoc in semis suis benignus remunerat et honorat, simplicitatem mundi cordis quo Deum cernimus, timorem dilectionis Domini quo probamur, credulam fidem mentis qua iustitiae deputamur. hanc fidem sequi, hunc Dei timorem seruare nos conuenit, qui custodientes uerba caelestia et sperantes promissa diuina filii Abrahae meruimus nuncupari. quod apostoli Pauli qui Dei uoce uas electionis est dictus contestatione firmatur dicentis: sicut Abraham credidit Deo, et accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam. cognoscite ergo quoniam qui ex fide sunt hi sunt filii Abrahae. hoc Iudaicus populus, cui a primordio legis monita loquebantur, incredulae mentis duritia et perfidi cordis insania seruare noluit, et ideo pro diffidentiae merito filiorum nomen amisit. non tamen omnium perfidae gentis aduersus nomen Domini, quominus intellegerent ueritatem, odio durata mens est. etiamque spiritus sanctus id est Christus Dominus noster qui profectus ex Deo patre uenit ut saluum faceret quod perierat Israelis: qui maior ac fortior ad subigenda contumacium colla in timorem sui nominis et potestatem eos qui aduersus sui luminationis claritatem obstinata etiam tunc mentis caecitate duras bant ad notitiam claritatis et gloriae suae tam facile conuertit, quam ut omnes saluos faceret prouidentia diuinae misericordiae suae dignatus aduenit.
thought_title: Abraham's faith as the model, and the Jewish people's rejection of it
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, showing that Abraham's believing faith is the model of the fear and faith that justify, and that the Jewish people lost the name of sons of Abraham by refusing this faith, though Christ came to save them.
pass_a_gloss: An example and a teaching of our fear and faith is shown from the faithful faith of the patriarch Abraham himself, who believed the promise of God immediately with a simple mind and therefore deserved that it be counted to him as righteousness with a worthy reward. God loves this, God seeks this, God in his seeds kindly rewards and honors this: the simplicity of a clean heart by which we see God, the fear of the love of the Lord by which we are approved, the believing faith of the mind by which we are counted for righteousness. It is fitting for us to follow this faith, to keep this fear of God, we who by keeping the heavenly words and hoping for the divine promises have deserved to be called sons of Abraham. This is confirmed by the testimony of the apostle Paul, who by the voice of God is called a vessel of election, saying: just as Abraham believed God, and it was accepted to him as righteousness. Know therefore that those who are of faith, these are sons of Abraham. The Jewish people, to whom the warnings of the law were spoken from the beginning, did not want to keep this because of the hardness of an unbeliving mind and the madness of a faithless heart, and therefore by the merit of their distrust they lost the name of sons. Yet the mind of not all of the faithless nation was hardened by hatred against the name of the Lord, so that they would not understand the truth. And also the Holy Spirit, that is Christ our Lord, who came forth from God the Father and came to save what had perished of Israel: he who is greater and stronger for subduing the necks of the stubborn into the fear of his name and his power, converted those who were hardening against the clarity of his light with the blindness of a mind still obstinate at that time to the knowledge of his clarity and glory as easily as he deigned to come by the providence of his divine mercy to save all.

choices.why: Keeps the glossary term credulitas as 'faith' and renders fidelis as 'faithful' to preserve the double emphasis on believing.
Literal rendering preserving the ablative of manner and the key term 'simple'.

choices.english: to be counted to him as righteousness
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'righteousness' and keeps the passive infinitive with dative of advantage.
Literal rendering of the unusual phrase; 'seeds' likely means descendants or offspring, but the literal sense is kept.

choices.english: the fear of the love of the Lord
choices.why: Keeps the genitive chain literal: fear of love, not fear and love.
rejected: the loving fear of the Lord
the fear and love of the Lord

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Pauline phrase, preserving 'election' rather than 'choice'.

bible_refs.note: sicut Abraham credidit Deo, et accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam
sicut Abraham credidit Deo, et accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam. cognoscite ergo quoniam qui ex fide sunt hi sunt filii Abrahae

pass_b_english: The example and pattern of our fear and faith is shown in the faithful faith of the patriarch Abraham himself, who believed God's promise at once with a simple mind, and therefore deserved by a fitting reward to be counted to him as righteousness. This is what God loves, this is what he seeks, this is what he in his kindness rewards and honors in his seeds: the simplicity of a pure heart by which we see God, the fear of the love of the Lord by which we are tested, the believing faith of the mind by which we are counted as righteousness. It is fitting for us to follow this faith and keep this fear of God, since by guarding the heavenly words and hoping in the divine promises we have deserved to be called sons of Abraham. This is confirmed by the testimony of the apostle Paul, who was called by God's voice a vessel of election, when he says: "Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. Know therefore that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham" (Galatians 3:6-7). The Jewish people, to whom the warnings of the law were spoken from the very beginning, refused to keep this because of the hardness of their unbelieving mind and the madness of their faithless heart, and therefore for their distrust they deserved to lose the name of sons. Yet not all of that faithless nation had their minds hardened by hatred against the name of the Lord so that they could not understand the truth. The Holy Spirit—that is, Christ our Lord, who came forth from God the Father and came to save what had been lost of Israel—he who is greater and stronger for bringing the necks of the stubborn under the fear of his name and his power, converted those who were hardening themselves against the brightness of his light with the blindness of a mind still obstinate to the knowledge of his brightness and glory as easily as he deigned to come in the providence of his divine mercy to save all.
notes: The phrase 'in semis suis' is unusual; 'semis' may be a corruption or variant of 'seminibus' (seeds) or 'semitis' (paths). The gloss keeps the literal reading 'in his seeds'.
The clause 'duras bant' appears to be a split or damaged form of 'durabant' (were hardening) or 'duraverant' (had hardened); the gloss renders it as 'were hardening' based on context.
The phrase 'quominus intellegerent ueritatem' is rendered literally as 'so that they would not understand the truth', preserving the negative purpose force.

problems.quote: and it was accepted to him as righteousness
problems.source_quote: et accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam
problems.why: Source says 'it was reckoned/credited to him'; 'accepted' misreads the participle as 'accepted' rather than 'reckoned.'
problems.fix: and it was reckoned to him as righteousness
problems.ruling: Latin 'et accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam' (likely 'creditur ei ad iustitiam') means 'credited to him as righteousness', not 'accepted to him'.

edits.old: and it was accepted to him as righteousness
edits.new: and it was reckoned to him as righteousness

fixed: Changed 'accepted' to 'reckoned' to match the source 'accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam', where 'accepto' is the passive participle of 'accipio' used in the sense of 'reckoned/credited' (as in Genesis 15:6 and Galatians 3:6).

problems.quote: when he says: "Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. Know therefore that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham" (Genesis 15:6; Galatians 3:6-7)
problems.source_quote: quod apostoli Pauli qui Dei uoce uas electionis est dictus contestatione firmatur dicentis: sicut Abraham credidit Deo, et accepto latum est ei ad iustitiam. cognoscite ergo quoniam qui ex fide sunt hi sunt filii Abrahae.
problems.why: The source only cites Paul’s words (Galatians 3:6‑7); Genesis 15:6 is not referenced.
problems.fix: when he says: "Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. Know therefore that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham" (Galatians 3:6‑7).
problems.ruling: Source attributes quote solely to Paul (Galatians 3:6-7); adding Genesis 15:6 misleads readers about the source's own scripture reference.

fixed: Removed Genesis 15:6 from the citation; the source only quotes Paul's words from Galatians 3:6-7.

last_rejected.quote: and hoping in the divine promises
last_rejected.why: 'sperantes' governs the accusative here meaning 'hoping for/expecting'; 'hoping in' changes sense.
last_rejected.fix: and hoping for the divine promises
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'sperantes promissa' means hoping for/promising, 'hoping in' is a minor nuance, not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: as easily as he deigned to come
last_rejected.why: Source says 'he converted them as easily as he deigned to come...'; English loses the verb 'converted'.
last_rejected.fix: as easily as he deigned to come in the providence of his divine mercy to save all, so he converted them
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'converted' and renders 'tam facile ... quam ut' correctly; no loss of the verb.
